ModMetaData.name: Rimfolk
ModMetaData.author: silvanalig
ModMetaData.description:
Their wishes. Their bonds. Their council. Their story.
Rimfolk turns your colonists into a society: people who want things, remember things, choose sides, keep traditions and write it all down. You lead them through a council, and they let you know what they think of it.
[b]A council that listens (or doesn't)[/b] Colonists voice wishes that fit who they are and what the colony can build: a room of their own, a hunt, a party, mercy for a prisoner, justice for one, help getting clean, a loved one rescued. Grant, promise, refuse or ignore them. Trust rises and falls, standards creep up while times are good, and a colonist who stays bitter long enough may walk out.
[b]Character, bonds and the social web[/b] Every colonist has a character, set by their traits and then marked by what happens to them, and it shows in every line they say. They talk about the raid, the council, the food and the newcomer, hold views that shift over time, and remember what they went through together. Groups form with names, roles and habits of their own; gossip spreads what people did, and the colony gives them a name for it. Friendships, rivalries, comrades-in-arms and mentorships form and change from what actually happens, and all of it feeds into votes, petitions and objections. Rarely, a long stretch of life changes a trait itself. With Ideology, faith comes into it too: who believes what and how firmly, talks and evenings of faith that can bring someone round, crises that shake it, and a council that can name one faith the colony's.
[b]Life goals[/b] Every colonist sets their heart on something: master a craft, marry, raise a child, earn a name, train a student, make peace with a rival. Reaching it is a moment the colony celebrates; dying before it is a loss the colony remembers.
[b]Secrets, vendettas and eulogies[/b] Colonists hide pasts that can come out at the worst moment; the bereaved swear vengeance on the factions that took their loved ones; and at every grave, someone who loved the dead speaks.
[b]Dreams[/b] Colonists wake from dreams about the raid, the friend they buried, the rival who insulted them, the dead they miss, and tell each other about them. Most are just a mood and a journal line; some leave an inspiration, a lesson, a shaken nerve or a softened grudge. And now and then a dream is an omen that comes true.
[b]Decrees, offices and elections[/b] Declare long hours, rationing, drills, austerity or festival days and watch who loves and who hates them. Colonists petition for decrees and to have them lifted. Every year the colony elects a speaker, marshal, quartermaster, physician and steward; overrule the vote at your peril.
[b]Dilemmas and traditions[/b] A thief in the stores, a feud, a pet that ate someone's dinner, the spoils of a raid, a child asking where the dead go: every answer costs someone. What the colony keeps choosing becomes tradition, and traditions are missed when broken.
[b]Memory[/b] Every colonist keeps a journal in their own voice. People earn names for what they do (the Healer, Deadeye, the Kindling). Anniversaries are marked, and each year someone writes the colony's annals.
[b]And the practical side[/b] Movable on-screen panels with every colonist's mood, the colony's vitals and the council at a glance, a hover card for any colonist, badges on the colonist bar for who needs you, and an advisor that ranks what the colony needs next and explains why, council meetings where colonists pitch ambitions and vote, whole-room plans you can place in one go, and an in-game almanac of the game's numbers and hard lessons.
Adapts to your tech level, research and DLCs (a medieval colony is never asked for turrets). Every part can be switched off or tuned in the settings.
[b]Requirements[/b] Requires Harmony. Works with or without any other mod; where a mod you use is present, Rimfolk reads it correctly and sometimes makes use of it.
